drafts.name: apriori-sparse-low-memory
drafts.title: Low-memory Apriori materializes large dense candidate blocks from sparse input
drafts.body:
#### Describe the bug

The sparse branch of `generate_new_combinations_low_memory` calls `toarray()` on both the prefix columns and all candidate columns before filtering matching rows. Thus `apriori(..., low_memory=True)` can allocate a block proportional to the full transaction count times the candidate count even when almost all entries are zero.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import tracemalloc
import numpy as np
from scipy import sparse
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns.apriori import generate_new_combinations_low_memory

X = sparse.csc_matrix(
    (np.ones(500, dtype=bool),
     (np.zeros(500, dtype=int), np.arange(500))),
    shape=(50000, 500),
)
tracemalloc.start()
first_support = next(generate_new_combinations_low_memory(
    np.arange(500).reshape(-1, 1), X, 1 / 50000, True
))
_, peak = tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
tracemalloc.stop()
print(X.nnz, first_support, peak)
```

#### Expected Results

Support counting should retain sparse storage and materialize only the one-dimensional row mask and support counts. The first pair occurs once.

#### Actual Results

The input has 500 nonzero entries, but evaluating the first prefix allocates a traced peak of **25,102,574 bytes**. The returned support is correctly 1; the avoidable allocation grows with both rows and candidates.

#### Proposed correction

Compute prefix row counts from the sparse submatrix, filter matching rows while still sparse, and sum the candidate columns without converting the block to a dense array. Keep candidate generation, pruning, ordering and the normalized support comparison unchanged. Add brute-force result comparisons and a regression that rejects dense sparse-matrix conversions.

The historical #619 introduced the present dense-block approach. #1179 changes candidate pruning and #1191 corrects support-boundary comparisons; neither removes this allocation.

#### Versions

Current master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, Linux, Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, pandas 2.3.3 and scikit-learn 1.8.0, using the frozen uv lock.

[Unmodified-source reproduction](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43864352542/job/133288951011).

drafts.name: minmax-finite-range
drafts.title: minmax_scaling returns NaN or infinity for finite input and output ranges
drafts.body:
#### Describe the bug

`minmax_scaling` subtracts the unscaled input extrema and computes `max_val - min_val` directly. Either intermediate range can overflow even when all input values, endpoints and expected scaled results are finite.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import numpy as np
from mlxtend.preprocessing import minmax_scaling

print(minmax_scaling(
    np.array([[-1e308], [0.], [1e308]]), columns=[0]
))
print(minmax_scaling(
    np.array([[0.], [0.5], [1.]]), columns=[0],
    min_val=-1e308, max_val=1e308
))
```

#### Expected Results

The first result is `[[0.], [0.5], [1.]]`. The second is `[[-1e308], [0.], [1e308]]`.

#### Actual Results

The first returns `[[0.], [0.], [nan]]`; the second returns `[[nan], [inf], [inf]]`, with floating-point warnings.

#### Proposed correction

Rescale only input columns whose extrema require it before forming their differences, and use a bounded weighted interpolation when the output range would overflow. Preserve ordinary-range arithmetic, constant-column handling, input containers and selected-column ordering. Regression tests should compare against high-precision references for finite opposite-sign extrema and cover ordinary, constant and mixed-range columns.

The single-changed-endpoint condition addressed by #1210 is a separate existing proposal; this report concerns overflowing arithmetic when the active input/output ranges are finite.

#### Versions

Current master `1aee767ef57b84a8191511a08955c583b65de382`, Linux, Python 3.11.18, NumPy 2.4.0, SciPy 1.16.3, pandas 2.3.3 and scikit-learn 1.8.0, using the frozen uv lock.

[Unmodified-source reproduction](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43864352542/job/133288951011).
